course.title: Barista and Coffee
course.tagline: Brew great coffee, steam milk and pour latte art like a cafe barista.

days.title: Coffee Basics: Beans, Water, and Tools
days.goal: Know what makes good coffee and what tools you need.

video.title: How to Make a Caffe Latte

steps: Coffee starts as beans. Fresh beans make the best coffee.
Grind means crush the beans into small bits. Fine grind is like sand. Coarse grind is like rough sugar.
Good coffee needs clean water. If your water tastes bad, your coffee will too.
Find your tools: a grinder, a kettle, a cup, and a spoon.
Taste black coffee, coffee with milk, and coffee with sugar. Note what you like.
days.task: List your coffee tools and taste three cups: black, with milk, and with sugar.
days.challenge: Write down which one you like best and why.

quiz.q: What does 'grind' mean?
options: To crush beans into small bits
quiz.explain: Grinding crushes beans into small bits so water can pull the flavour out.

quiz.q: Why does water matter for coffee?
quiz.explain: Coffee is mostly water, so the water's taste matters a lot.

quiz.q: What is the difference between fine and coarse grind?
options: Fine is like sand, coarse is like rough sugar
quiz.explain: Fine grind is powdery like sand. Coarse grind is chunky like rough sugar.

days.title: Your First French Press Coffee
days.goal: Brew coffee with a French press, the easiest way.

video.title: Latte Art for Beginners: 12 Easy Designs (Step-by-Step Tutorial)

steps: A French press is a jug with a plunger that pushes the grounds down.
Add coarse coffee grounds to the press.
Pour hot water over them. Stir gently.
Put the lid on and wait 4 minutes.
Push the plunger down slowly and pour.
days.task: Brew a French press coffee.
days.challenge: Brew a second cup with more coffee and compare the strength.

quiz.q: What is a French press?
options: A jug with a plunger that pushes grounds down
quiz.explain: A French press is a jug with a plunger that separates the coffee from the grounds.

quiz.q: How long does French press coffee brew?
quiz.explain: Four minutes is the standard time for a French press.

quiz.q: Why push the plunger down slowly?
options: Fast pushing stirs the grounds back into the coffee
quiz.explain: A slow push keeps the grounds at the bottom.

days.title: Espresso: The Heart of Cafe Coffee
days.goal: Pull a good espresso shot.

video.title: Latte Art For Beginners: How To Pour Heart

steps: Espresso is strong coffee made by pushing hot water through fine grounds.
A shot is one small serving of espresso, about 30ml.
Fill the portafilter (the handle with the basket) with fine coffee.
Tamp means press the coffee down flat and even.
Lock it in and start the water. A good shot takes about 25 seconds.
days.task: Pull an espresso shot.
days.challenge: Taste it. Note if it is sour (too fast) or bitter (too slow).

quiz.q: What is espresso?
options: Strong coffee made by pushing hot water through fine grounds
quiz.explain: Espresso is made by forcing hot water through finely ground coffee.

quiz.q: What does 'tamp' mean?
options: To press the coffee down flat and even
quiz.explain: Tamping presses the grounds flat so water flows through evenly.

quiz.q: How long should a good shot take?
quiz.explain: About 25 seconds gives a balanced shot.

days.title: Steaming Milk: Smooth and Silky
days.goal: Steam milk until it is smooth and glossy.

video.title: How to Make Latte Art Step by Step | From Grinder to Tulip Latte Art

steps: Steamed milk is milk heated with steam until it is hot and smooth.
Microfoam is milk with tiny bubbles. It looks like wet paint.
Fill the jug one-third full with cold milk.
Put the steam wand just under the surface. Turn on the steam.
Listen for a soft hissing sound. Stop when the jug feels hot to touch.
days.task: Steam a jug of milk until it is smooth and glossy.
days.challenge: Practise twice: once for a latte, once for a cappuccino.

quiz.q: What is microfoam?
options: Milk with tiny bubbles that looks like wet paint
quiz.explain: Microfoam is smooth milk with tiny bubbles. It pours like paint.

quiz.q: How full should the milk jug be?
quiz.explain: One-third full leaves room for the milk to grow as it steams.

quiz.q: When do you stop steaming?
options: When the jug feels hot to touch
quiz.explain: Hot to touch means the milk is about the right heat.

days.title: Your First Latte
days.goal: Make a latte: espresso plus steamed milk.

video.title: How To Pour a Heart: Latte Art

steps: A latte is espresso with lots of steamed milk and a little foam.
Pull a double shot of espresso into a cup.
Steam the milk until smooth and glossy.
Pour the milk slowly into the espresso.
Hold back the foam with a spoon, then add a little on top.
days.task: Make a latte.
days.challenge: Make a second latte and try pouring a simple heart.

quiz.q: What is a latte?
options: Espresso with lots of steamed milk and a little foam
quiz.explain: A latte is mostly steamed milk with espresso and a little foam.

quiz.q: Why pour milk slowly?
options: Slow pouring mixes the milk and coffee well
quiz.explain: A slow pour mixes milk and espresso into a smooth drink.

quiz.q: Why hold back the foam with a spoon?
options: So the foam goes on top at the end
quiz.explain: Holding the foam back lets the milk mix first, then the foam sits on top.

days.title: Choosing the Right Milk
days.goal: Pick the best milk for lattes and latte art.

video.title: How To Pour a Tulip: Latte Art

steps: Whole milk makes the best microfoam. It is rich and smooth.
Skimmed milk makes big bubbles and is harder to pour.
Oat milk is a good non-dairy choice. It steams well.
Always use cold milk. Warm milk does not foam well.
Taste a latte made with each milk and pick your favourite.
days.task: Make lattes with whole milk, skimmed milk, and oat milk.
days.challenge: Write down which milk foams best and which tastes best.

quiz.q: Which milk makes the best microfoam?
quiz.explain: Whole milk has the fat and protein that make smooth microfoam.

quiz.q: Why use cold milk for steaming?
options: Cold milk foams better than warm milk
quiz.explain: Cold milk gives you more time to build foam before it gets too hot.

quiz.q: Which non-dairy milk steams well?
quiz.explain: Oat milk steams well and tastes good in coffee.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Coffee Tasting
days.goal: Make three coffees and taste them side by side.

video.title: How To Pour a Rosetta: Latte Art

steps: Make a French press coffee, an espresso, and a latte.
Serve them in small cups so tasters can try all three.
Write a tasting note for each: strong, smooth, bitter, or sweet.
Ask tasters which one they like best and why.
Pick your favourite and write the recipe down.
days.task: Make three coffees and hold a tasting for your household.
days.challenge: Write tasting notes for each coffee.

quiz.q: Why taste three coffees side by side?
quiz.explain: Tasting side by side makes the differences in taste clear.

quiz.q: What is a tasting note?
options: A short note on how a coffee tastes
quiz.explain: A tasting note is a short description of the flavour.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe for your favourite?
options: So you can make it the same way every time
quiz.explain: A written recipe lets you repeat a good coffee.

project.title: Hold a Coffee Tasting
project.brief: Make a French press, an espresso, and a latte, and taste them side by side.
checks: Tasting notes written for all three

days.title: Cappuccino: Equal Parts
days.goal: Make a cappuccino: equal parts espresso, milk, and foam.

video.title: 3 Easy Latte Art Designs: Heart

steps: A cappuccino is one-third espresso, one-third steamed milk, one-third foam.
Pull a double shot into a small cup.
Steam the milk with more air than a latte, so it is thick and foamy.
Pour the milk, then spoon the thick foam on top.
Dust with cocoa or cinnamon if you like.
days.task: Make a cappuccino.
days.challenge: Make a latte and a cappuccino side by side and compare.

quiz.q: What is a cappuccino?
options: Equal parts espresso, steamed milk, and foam
quiz.explain: A cappuccino is one-third espresso, one-third milk, and one-third foam.

quiz.q: How is cappuccino milk different from latte milk?
options: It has more air, so it is thick and foamy
quiz.explain: Cappuccino milk is steamed with more air, so it is thick and foamy.

quiz.q: What can you dust on a cappuccino?
quiz.explain: Cocoa or cinnamon on top is the classic finish.

days.title: Latte Art: Your First Heart
days.goal: Pour a heart in a latte.

video.title: Rosetta

steps: Latte art is a pattern made by pouring steamed milk into espresso.
Start with smooth, glossy milk. No big bubbles.
Pour from high up to mix the milk in.
Lower the jug close to the cup and pour a little more milk.
Lift the jug up and pull through to make the heart shape.
days.task: Pour a heart in a latte.
days.challenge: Practise 5 hearts and keep the best one.

quiz.q: What is latte art?
options: A pattern made by pouring steamed milk into espresso
quiz.explain: Latte art is a pattern formed by pouring milk into espresso.

quiz.q: Why pour from high up first?
options: It mixes the milk into the coffee
quiz.explain: Pouring from high up mixes the milk in before you draw the pattern.

quiz.q: What makes a good heart?
options: Smooth milk and a steady pour
quiz.explain: Smooth milk and a slow, steady pour make a clean heart.

days.title: Latte Art: The Tulip
days.goal: Pour a tulip in a latte.

video.title: Bear latte art

steps: A tulip is a stack of hearts, one on top of another.
Pour a small heart, stop, then pour another above it.
Repeat 2 or 3 times to build the stack.
Pull through the middle at the end to join them.
Practise on water with a drop of soap if you want to save milk.
days.task: Pour a tulip in a latte.
days.challenge: Pour a heart and a tulip side by side and compare.

quiz.q: What is a tulip in latte art?
options: A stack of hearts, one on top of another
quiz.explain: A tulip is made by stacking hearts on top of each other.

quiz.q: How do you build a tulip?
options: Pour a small heart, stop, then pour another above it
quiz.explain: A tulip is built by pouring one heart, stopping, then pouring another above it.

quiz.q: Why practise on water with soap?
options: It saves milk while you learn
quiz.explain: Water with soap acts like milk, so you can practise without wasting milk.

days.title: Latte Art: The Rosetta
days.goal: Pour a rosetta, the leaf pattern.

video.title: Choosing the Right Milk for Your Latte

steps: A rosetta looks like a leaf or a fern.
Pour from low down and wiggle the jug side to side.
Move the jug back slowly as you wiggle.
Pull through the middle at the end to make the stem.
Practise slowly. Speed comes later.
days.task: Pour a rosetta in a latte.
days.challenge: Pour a heart, a tulip, and a rosetta, and pick your best.

quiz.q: What does a rosetta look like?
quiz.explain: A rosetta looks like a leaf or a fern.

quiz.q: How do you make a rosetta?
options: Wiggle the jug side to side while moving back slowly
quiz.explain: A side-to-side wiggle while moving back makes the leaf shape.

quiz.q: Why practise slowly?
options: Slow practice builds control. Speed comes later
quiz.explain: Slow, careful practice builds the control you need.

days.title: The Perfect Pitcher
days.goal: Pick the right milk pitcher for latte art.

video.title: What Type of Pitcher is Best for Latte Art?

steps: A pitcher is the metal jug you steam milk in.
A small pitcher is best for one cup. A big one is for many cups.
A pitcher with a pointed spout pours thin lines for art.
A round spout is fine for normal lattes.
Keep your pitcher clean. Old milk ruins new milk.
days.task: Steam milk in two different pitchers and compare the pour.
days.challenge: Pick the pitcher you like best and use it all week.

quiz.q: What is a milk pitcher?
options: The metal jug you steam milk in
quiz.explain: A pitcher is the metal jug used to steam and pour milk.

quiz.q: Why does the spout shape matter?
options: A pointed spout pours thin lines for latte art
quiz.explain: A pointed spout gives a thin, controlled pour for art.

quiz.q: Why keep the pitcher clean?
options: Old milk ruins the taste of new milk
quiz.explain: Leftover milk goes sour and spoils fresh milk.

days.title: Espresso Drinks Menu
days.goal: Learn the main espresso drinks and how they differ.

video.title: Making the Perfect Latte Microfoam

steps: Espresso: just a shot, no milk.
Latte: lots of milk, little foam.
Cappuccino: equal parts espresso, milk, and foam.
Flat white: espresso with thin, smooth milk and almost no foam.
Mocha: latte with chocolate.
days.task: Make a flat white and a mocha.
days.challenge: Make all five drinks and line them up for a photo.

quiz.q: What is a flat white?
options: Espresso with thin, smooth milk and almost no foam
quiz.explain: A flat white has thin, smooth milk and very little foam.

quiz.q: What is a mocha?
quiz.explain: A mocha is a latte with chocolate added.

quiz.q: How is a latte different from a cappuccino?
options: A latte has more milk and less foam
quiz.explain: A latte has lots of milk and little foam. A cappuccino has equal parts.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Cafe Menu
days.goal: Make a cafe menu with five drinks.

video.title: Extract the Perfect Espresso

steps: Pick five drinks: espresso, latte, cappuccino, flat white, and mocha.
Write the recipes with exact amounts.
Make all five and serve them in nice cups.
Add a latte art heart to the latte.
Ask tasters to pick a favourite and set a price for each drink.
days.task: Make a five-drink cafe menu.
days.challenge: Price each drink as if you were selling it.

quiz.q: Why make five drinks?
options: A menu with five choices shows your range
quiz.explain: Five drinks show you can run a real cafe menu.

quiz.q: Why add latte art to the latte?
options: Art makes the drink look professional
quiz.explain: Latte art shows skill and makes the drink look worth buying.

quiz.q: Why price each drink?
options: So you know what to charge and what you earn
quiz.explain: Pricing tells you the profit on each drink.

project.title: Make a Five-Drink Cafe Menu
project.brief: Make espresso, latte, cappuccino, flat white, and mocha.
checks: Latte art heart on the latte

days.title: Coffee Beans: Origins and Roasts
days.goal: Learn how beans and roasts change the taste.

video.title: The Simplest Latte Pattern: The Heart!

steps: Beans come from different countries and taste different.
Light roast keeps more of the bean's own taste. It can be fruity.
Dark roast tastes stronger and more bitter.
Medium roast is in the middle and suits most people.
Taste a light and a dark roast side by side.
days.task: Taste a light roast and a dark roast side by side.
days.challenge: Write down which roast you like best and why.

quiz.q: What does light roast taste like?
options: More of the bean's own taste, sometimes fruity
quiz.explain: Light roast keeps the bean's own flavour, which can be fruity.

quiz.q: What does dark roast taste like?
quiz.explain: Dark roast tastes stronger and more bitter.

quiz.q: Which roast suits most people?
quiz.explain: Medium roast is balanced and suits most people.

days.title: Grinding Coffee: Fine or Coarse
days.goal: Grind coffee the right way for each method.

video.title: James Hoffmann French Press Method

steps: French press needs coarse grind, like rough sugar.
Espresso needs fine grind, like sand.
Too fine for a French press makes muddy coffee.
Too coarse for espresso makes weak, sour coffee.
Grind just before brewing. Ground coffee goes stale fast.
days.task: Grind coffee coarse for a French press and fine for espresso.
days.challenge: Brew both and compare the taste.

quiz.q: What grind does a French press need?
quiz.explain: A French press needs coarse grounds so they do not slip through the filter.

quiz.q: What grind does espresso need?
quiz.explain: Espresso needs fine grounds so the water pulls out lots of flavour fast.

quiz.q: Why grind just before brewing?
quiz.explain: Ground coffee loses flavour quickly. Fresh grinding keeps it tasty.

days.title: Iced Coffee and Cold Brew
days.goal: Make iced coffee and cold brew.

video.title: How to Make a Caffe Latte

steps: Iced coffee is hot coffee poured over ice.
Cold brew is coffee steeped in cold water for 12 hours.
Cold brew tastes smooth and less bitter.
Make cold brew: coarse grounds plus cold water in a jar, wait 12 hours, strain.
Serve both over ice with milk if you like.
days.task: Make iced coffee.
days.challenge: Start a cold brew tonight and drink it tomorrow.

quiz.q: What is cold brew?
options: Coffee steeped in cold water for 12 hours
quiz.explain: Cold brew is coffee left in cold water for 12 hours.

quiz.q: How does cold brew taste?
quiz.explain: Cold water pulls out less bitterness, so cold brew tastes smooth.

quiz.q: What is iced coffee?
quiz.explain: Iced coffee is hot coffee cooled by pouring it over ice.

days.title: Flavoured Lattes: Vanilla and Caramel
days.goal: Make vanilla and caramel lattes.

video.title: Latte Art for Beginners: 12 Easy Designs (Step-by-Step Tutorial)

steps: A flavoured latte is a latte with syrup added.
Add syrup to the espresso before the milk.
Vanilla syrup adds a sweet, soft taste.
Caramel syrup adds a rich, sweet taste.
Start with a small amount. You can add more.
days.task: Make a vanilla latte.
days.challenge: Make a caramel latte and compare.

quiz.q: When do you add syrup to a latte?
options: To the espresso before the milk
quiz.explain: Syrup goes into the espresso first so it mixes well.

quiz.q: What does vanilla syrup add?
quiz.explain: Vanilla adds a sweet, soft taste.

quiz.q: Why start with a small amount of syrup?
options: You can add more but you cannot take it out
quiz.explain: Too much syrup makes a drink too sweet. Start small.

days.title: Costing Coffee: Price Your Drinks
days.goal: Work out what each coffee costs and what to charge.

video.title: Latte Art For Beginners: How To Pour Heart

steps: List every ingredient: beans, milk, sugar, and cups.
Add the cost of the cup and packaging.
Divide the total by the number of drinks you made.
Charge 3 to 4 times the cost for a profit.
Compare with cafes near you.
days.task: Cost a latte and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost a cappuccino the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per drink?
options: Total cost divided by the number of drinks
quiz.explain: Cost per drink is the total cost shared across all the drinks you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 3 to 4 times the cost?
options: To cover rent, power, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: Cafes have rent and power costs, so drinks are priced higher than home costs.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Cups and packaging are real costs of every drink.

days.title: Coffee Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest coffee problems.

video.title: How to Make Latte Art Step by Step | From Grinder to Tulip Latte Art

steps: Espresso is sour? The shot was too fast. Grind finer.
Espresso is bitter? The shot was too slow. Grind coarser.
Milk has big bubbles? You added too much air. Steam it smoother.
Latte art will not form? The milk is not smooth enough. Practise steaming.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one coffee problem you have had.
days.challenge: Pull three shots and note the time of each one.

quiz.q: Why is espresso sour?
quiz.explain: A fast shot does not pull out enough flavour, so it tastes sour.

quiz.q: Why is espresso bitter?
quiz.explain: A slow shot pulls out too much, so it tastes bitter.

quiz.q: Why does milk have big bubbles?
options: Too much air was added while steaming
quiz.explain: Too much air makes big bubbles. Gentle steaming makes tiny ones.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Coffee Morning
days.goal: Run a coffee morning for friends or family.

video.title: How To Pour a Heart: Latte Art

steps: Pick the menu: latte, cappuccino, flat white, and iced coffee.
Write the recipes, costs, and prices.
Set up your coffee station the night before.
Make each drink to order and serve it hot.
Ask guests to vote for their favourite.
days.task: Run a coffee morning for at least 4 people.
days.challenge: Cost the morning and work out your profit if you sold the drinks.

quiz.q: Why set up the night before?
quiz.explain: Setting up early means no rushing when guests arrive.

quiz.q: Why make drinks to order?
quiz.explain: Coffee made to order is hot and fresh.

quiz.q: Why ask guests to vote?
options: Votes tell you which drinks sell best
quiz.explain: Votes show you which drinks to keep on your menu.

project.title: Run a Coffee Morning
project.brief: Serve latte, cappuccino, flat white, and iced coffee to at least 4 people.
checks: Four different drinks made to order
Each drink made fresh and hot
Latte art on at least one drink

days.title: Cleaning Your Coffee Equipment
days.goal: Clean your grinder, machine, and pitchers.

video.title: How To Pour a Tulip: Latte Art

steps: Clean the portafilter after every shot. Old coffee tastes bitter.
Wipe the steam wand after every use. Milk burns onto it fast.
Wash pitchers with hot water and soap.
Clean the grinder once a week. Old grounds go stale.
Descale the machine when the manual says so.
days.task: Clean all your coffee equipment today.
days.challenge: Write a cleaning list and stick it near your coffee station.

quiz.q: Why clean the portafilter after every shot?
quiz.explain: Leftover coffee goes stale and makes the next shot bitter.

quiz.q: Why wipe the steam wand after every use?
quiz.explain: Milk dries and burns onto a hot wand in minutes.

quiz.q: Why clean the grinder weekly?
options: Old grounds go stale and spoil new coffee
quiz.explain: Stale grounds in the grinder spoil fresh coffee.

days.title: Serving Customers: The Barista Way
days.goal: Serve coffee like a professional barista.

video.title: How To Pour a Rosetta: Latte Art

steps: Greet the customer with a smile and their name if you know it.
Repeat the order back so you get it right.
Make the drink fresh. Do not let it sit.
Serve it hot with a smile. Ask if they want anything else.
Thank them and invite them back.
days.task: Practise serving coffee to a friend, step by step.
days.challenge: Ask your friend what made the service feel good.

quiz.q: Why repeat the order back?
quiz.explain: Repeating the order stops mistakes.

quiz.q: Why serve coffee fresh?
options: Coffee tastes best hot and fresh
quiz.explain: Coffee left sitting goes cold and bitter.

quiz.q: Why use the customer's name?
quiz.explain: Using a name makes service feel personal.

days.title: Your Signature Coffee
days.goal: Choose and perfect one coffee you can make brilliantly.

video.title: 3 Easy Latte Art Designs: Heart

steps: Pick the coffee your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Make it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and make it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Make your signature coffee and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Make it for someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature coffee?
options: A coffee you can make brilliantly every time
A coffee with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature coffee is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Coffee Business: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling coffee.

video.title: Rosetta

steps: Pick 3 or 4 drinks to sell. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your drinks in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you buy only what you need.
days.task: Take photos of your best coffees and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 drinks?
options: A small menu is easier to make well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you buy only what you need and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell coffee.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your coffee business.

video.title: Bear latte art

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which drinks sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for coffee separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one coffee morning.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to make
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for beans, milk, and cups.

quiz.q: Why keep coffee money separate?
options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Latte Art Practice: Fun Designs
days.goal: Try fun latte art designs like a bear.

video.title: Choosing the Right Milk for Your Latte

steps: Start with the heart. It is the base of most designs.
A bear is a heart with two small ears on top.
Pour the ears first, then the heart below.
Use a toothpick to add small details like eyes.
Practise on water with soap to save milk.
days.task: Pour a bear in a latte.
days.challenge: Try one more fun design of your choice.

quiz.q: What is the base of most latte art?
quiz.explain: The heart is the base. Tulips and bears build on it.

quiz.q: How do you make a bear?
options: Pour two small ears, then a heart below
quiz.explain: A bear is two small ears poured above a heart.

quiz.q: Why practise on water with soap?
options: It saves milk while you learn
quiz.explain: Water with soap acts like milk, so you can practise without wasting milk.

days.title: Coffee and Food Pairing
days.goal: Pair coffee with food that suits it.

video.title: What Type of Pitcher is Best for Latte Art?

steps: Black coffee goes well with sweet cakes and pastries.
A latte goes well with a light breakfast.
Iced coffee goes well with a sandwich on a hot day.
Serve a small biscuit with every coffee.
Ask tasters what food they like with each coffee.
days.task: Serve a coffee with a cake or biscuit and note the pairing.
days.challenge: Try three pairings and pick the best one.

quiz.q: What goes well with black coffee?
quiz.explain: Sweet cakes balance the bitterness of black coffee.

quiz.q: Why serve a biscuit with coffee?
options: A small sweet bite goes well with coffee
quiz.explain: A biscuit adds a sweet bite that suits coffee.

quiz.q: What goes well with iced coffee?
options: A sandwich on a hot day
quiz.explain: Iced coffee and a sandwich make a light, cool lunch.

days.title: Revision: The Barista's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: Making the Perfect Latte Microfoam

steps: Pull an espresso shot from memory, without help.
Steam milk until smooth and glossy.
Pour a heart in a latte.
Name the five main espresso drinks.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Make a full cafe menu from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one coffee skill from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What are the five main espresso drinks?
options: Espresso, latte, cappuccino, flat white, mocha
quiz.explain: Espresso, latte, cappuccino, flat white, and mocha are the five main drinks.

quiz.q: Why make drinks from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Making drinks without a recipe shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Cafe Day
days.goal: Plan your capstone cafe day and gather everything you need.

video.title: Extract the Perfect Espresso

steps: Choose your capstone menu: five drinks, including latte art.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the making order, starting with what takes longest.
Check you have every tool and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest drink if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone drink today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: espresso, milk, latte art, and costing
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why start with what takes longest?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Long tasks start first so all drinks are ready together.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real day
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Barista's Cafe Day: Five Drinks, Served Like a Pro
capstone.brief: Run a small cafe day for your household or customers: serve espresso, latte, cappuccino, flat white, and mocha, with latte art on at least two drinks. Cost every drink, serve them hot and on time, and collect feedback.
checks: Menu planned with recipes, costs, and prices
Espresso shots pulled well, not sour or bitter
Latte art poured on at least two drinks
Drinks served hot and on time
Costs worked out and profit known
Feedback collected from at least one person who drank the coffee
deliverables: A photo of your cafe menu and drinks
Your written menu with recipes, costs, and prices
Your making order, starting with what takes longest
Your signature coffee recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
